html:
The Viceroyalty of Brazil is the name for colonial Portuguese Brazil in the years when its governors held the title of viceroy. Some earlier governors had used it, but from 1763 every governor did, and that year the capital moved from Salvador to Rio de Janeiro.

The move followed the gold. The gold rush in Minas Gerais had pulled people and money south, and Rio was the port for the mines. Under the Marquis of Pombal in Lisbon the colony was run more tightly, and the Jesuits were expelled in 1759.

Brazil grew restless. A plot for independence in Minas Gerais was crushed in 1789, and its leader Tiradentes was hanged in 1792. Then in 1808 the Portuguese court fled to Brazil from Napoleon's armies, making Rio the capital of the whole empire. In 1815 Brazil was raised to a kingdom equal with Portugal, ending the viceroyalty. Independent Brazil followed in 1822.
